newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen falling.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to fall slightly on a proposed sale of 30,000 tonnes of basmati rice by the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) on Sunday, dealers said on Thursday.
A dealer said the auction for 30,000 tonnes rice would be made through open bids to be received by the RECP on Sunday.
He said rice prices were likely to fall in the next few weeks as the IRRI-6 variety had reached the market in southern Pakistan and basmati would reach the market early next month.
The IRRI-6 export price was not quoted as it was not available in large quantities, an RECP official said.
He said Basmati rice fell to $433.75 per tonne due to the last month's auction of 10,000 tonnes basmati rice at $433.75 per tonne FOB.

Pakistan's 1996/97 (July-June) rice production target has been fixed at 4.2 million tonnes against 3.8 million in 1995/96 and dealers said the crop was likely to give an exportable surplus of more than 1.5 million tonnes.
